skill.description: Frontend development guidelines for Next.js 15 applications using React 19, TypeScript, Shadcn/ui, and Tailwind CSS. The skill covers component patterns, App Router structure, data fetching, styling, performance, and TypeScript conventions.
skill.summary: Guide Next.js 15 frontend work with React 19, TypeScript, Shadcn/ui, and Tailwind CSS patterns.

security_audit.summary: All 86 static findings were reviewed against SKILL.md and judged false positives. The external command detections are Markdown backticks and code fences, the network detection is a placeholder example, and no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: - [ ] Add `"use client"` directive only if needed (interactivity, hooks, browser APIs)
- **Server Components** (default): No `"use client"`, can fetch data directly, smaller bundle
- **Client Components**: Add `"use client"` for interactivity, hooks, browser APIs
- No need for `useEffect` or data fetching libraries
- Customize via `className` prop or CSS variables
2. **App Router Structure**: Use file-based routing with `app/` directory
8. **Import Aliases**: Use `@/` prefix for clean imports

content.user_title: Build Next.js Frontends With Clear Guidelines
content.value_statement: Modern Next.js projects need consistent component, routing, and data fetching patterns. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical React 19 and TypeScript conventions.
actual_capabilities: Provides checklists for new Next.js components and pages.
Explains Server Component and Client Component selection.
Documents App Router file organization and import aliases.
Shows patterns for Server Actions, data fetching, loading, and error states.
Gives Tailwind CSS and Shadcn/ui styling guidance.
Includes TypeScript and performance conventions for React 19 projects.
limitations: Does not run code, install packages, or validate a project automatically.
Examples use placeholder APIs and must be adapted before production.
Focuses on Next.js 15, React 19, Shadcn/ui, and Tailwind CSS.
Does not replace framework documentation for version-specific changes.

use_cases.title: Create Consistent Components
use_cases.description: Apply Server Component defaults, Client Component rules, typed props, and Shadcn/ui imports when building reusable UI.

use_cases.title: Plan App Router Pages
use_cases.description: Structure routes, loading states, error boundaries, metadata, and feature folders for a Next.js application.

use_cases.title: Review Frontend Conventions
use_cases.description: Check React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and performance choices before merging frontend changes.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend development guidelines to plan a new profile card component for a Next.js 15 app.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Page Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline the files and patterns for a posts page with loading and error states.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Data Fetching
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my data fetching approach for a Next.js App Router page and suggest Server Component or Server Action improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Frontend Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my frontend structure against these guidelines and identify routing, typing, styling, and performance improvements.

output_examples.input: Create a new posts page with loading and error handling.
output: A recommended App Router file structure for the posts route.
Guidance to fetch data in the page Server Component.
Separate notes for loading UI, error boundary behavior, and metadata.

output_examples.input: Review whether a component should use the client directive.
output: A decision based on hooks, interactivity, and browser API usage.
A recommendation to keep the component server-rendered when possible.
Notes on where Shadcn/ui client components can be imported safely.

output_examples.input: Improve frontend TypeScript and styling consistency.
output: Suggestions for explicit prop interfaces and strict TypeScript usage.
Tailwind CSS guidance using the shared class name helper.
Advice to keep reusable UI separate from feature-specific components.

best_practices: Default to Server Components unless interactivity, hooks, or browser APIs require Client Components.
Keep routes, loading states, error boundaries, and feature files aligned with App Router conventions.
Use typed props, Shadcn/ui components, Tailwind CSS utilities, and shared import aliases consistently.
anti_patterns: Adding the client directive to every component without checking whether it is needed.
Mixing route-specific feature code into global reusable component folders.
Using untyped props, generic any types, or ad hoc class string logic.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Next.js 15, React 19, TypeScript, Shadcn/ui, and Tailwind CSS.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready components?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and examples, but generated code still needs project-specific review and testing.

faq.question: Does it support both Claude and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it execute commands or install dependencies?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a Markdown guideline and does not execute commands by itself.

faq.question: When should I use Client Components?
faq.answer: Use them for interactivity, React hooks, browser APIs, or client-only UI behavior.

faq.question: Does it include backend API guidance?
faq.answer: No. It references related backend guidance but focuses on frontend patterns and page structure.
